question: Björn Seibert and Alexander Winterstein – who was promoted to director in DG COMM in an astoundingly timely manner – will be, as we have learned, granted leave until the end of Ursula von der Leyen’s election campaign on 10 June 2024. Ursula von der Leyen is not listed as a candidate on any ballot paper. Instead, she wishes to be reappointed by the heads of government later in November 2024. 1.
How can the Commission President justify this temporary leave of absence on the basis of the elections to the European Parliament?
Do Björn Seibert and Alexander Winterstein also have to clear their desks in the Commission?
Where and with what resources are they running their campaign for the incumbent President?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (30.7.2024) Mr Björn Seibert and Mr Alexander Winterstein have taken a temporary unpaid leave on personal grounds from their duties in the Commission to support the European Parliament election campaign of the European People’s Party in a private capacity. This ensures a clear separation between external activities and institutional duties.

The appropriate procedures were followed for authorising these activities: their declarations were assessed based on the applicable rules, notably the Staff Regulations and the Conditions of Employment of Other Servants, the Commission Decision on outside activities1 C(2018)4048 final and the recently adopted Commission Decision on the conduct of officials and other servants during the election campaign to the European Parliament C(2024)1746 final (the ‘EP Election Decision’)2.

Mr Seibert and Mr Winterstein do not have any access to or use of Commission’s resources for the entire duration of their unpaid leave. In accordance with the applicable rules and the EP Election Decision, staff members must not use any of the Commission’s services or human or material resources for the purpose of a political campaign.
